chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Studying with Frank Lanham in Chicago
summary: Lanham taught him fundamentals and writing in the Electrum style instead of classical guitar, and introduced him to classical guitar history.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Everything -- Frank -- and they didn't spell my teacher's name. His name was Lanham. He was a very marvelous -- he was a marvelous man. Frank Lanham. I'll tell you, I studied with this man in Chicago, and he wanted to teach me classical guitar, and I didn't want to play classical guitar, and I wouldn't -- I wouldn't take classical guitar so he taught me the Electrum style. And you couldn't -- you had to write, you see, when you studied with him you had to also write. He taught you really the fundamentals of music, and I enjoyed it very much.

But I -- he never knew how old the classical guitar was until I started studying with him, and so I was there taking a lesson one day, and an old black man came in, this guy looked like he was about 80. He was -- well, he was in his eighties. Very stately and well groomed, and he and Mr. Lanham started talking and it was very interesting to hear them talk. They had toured Europe. I forgot this guy's name, playing the classical guitar. Years before. Now this was in the thirties, you know, and I was amazed, because I didn't know the history of the classical guitar. In later years I took up classical guitar.
He also taught I think this guy's name is Albert Pick, who was -- he's quite a guitarist, he's quite a classical

guitarist. And he lives in Chicago, but at this time that he was teaching Pick he was trying to get me to take classical guitar. But I was working with Roy at the time, at the Three Duces, and I wasn't interested. You know, I was thinking of jazz then you know. I was working with Zuty and all of the-- the real jazz men. And that was -- I just went to him, for musicianship, really, you know.
Frank Lanham, a great teacher. He died -- he used to come down to hear me play.
